model_plain: Most people vote in person at their assigned polling place on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 7 AM to 7 PM. Alabama has no early voting. If you can't be there that day and have one of the legal excuses, you can vote absentee by mail or in person at your county's absentee office.

deadlines.rule: Register or update your registration online by 11:59 PM on Monday, October 19. The official Voter Guide: 'If registering to vote electronically, registration must be submitted before 11:59 PM on the registration deadline.' Online registration only works 'if they have a valid Alabama Driver's License or Non-Driver ID card.'

A paper form 'must be postmarked no later than the registration deadline,' Monday, October 19. Forms are at Probate Judge and License Commissioner offices, libraries, schools, or printable from alabamavotes.gov; mail to your county Board of Registrars.

In person, 'registration must be received before the close of business of the registration deadline,' Monday, October 19, at your county Board of Registrars. Mobile County Board of Registrars: 151 Government St, Suite 165, Mobile 36602, (251) 574-8586.

registration.same_day_notes: Alabama has no same-day or Election Day registration. Registration is 'closed during the 14 days prior to an election and on Election Day.' If you are not registered by October 19, you cannot vote in this election. One exception: if you moved within your county and didn't update in time, you can go to your NEW polling place, update your registration there, and cast a provisional ballot.
registration.still_possible_now: No. Registration for this election closed Monday, October 19, and Alabama has no same-day registration. Check your status at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov. One exception: if you moved within your county and didn't update in time, go to your new polling place, update there and vote a provisional ballot.

mail_ballot.who_gets_one: Nobody gets one automatically. You must apply, and you must check one of the legal excuses on the application. The excuses, per the Secretary of State: you expect to be absent from the county on Election Day; you are ill or have a physical infirmity that keeps you from your polling place; you are a registered Alabama voter living outside the county (military, overseas, students away at school, and their spouses or dependents); you are an appointed poll worker or poll watcher assigned somewhere other than your own precinct; you expect to work a required shift of at least 10 hours that overlaps the 7 AM to 7 PM polling hours; you are a caregiver for a family member (to the second degree of kinship) who is confined to their home; or you are in prison or jail and have not been convicted of a felony involving moral turpitude. Absentee voting opened September 9, 2026. Send the application to your county Absentee Election Manager, which is 'usually the Circuit Clerk.' There is no permanent absentee list for most voters; apply every election. (Voters with a permanent disability can file one physician-notarized application per calendar year.)

request_deadline.rule: Mailed applications must be received by the Absentee Election Manager by Tuesday, October 27 (7 days before the election). The SOS press release: 'county absentee election managers must receive mail-in absentee ballot applications by Tuesday, October 27, 2026.' In-person applications: Thursday, October 29 (5 days before), returned by the voter in person. If you apply in person you can vote your absentee ballot right there in the same visit. Include a copy of your photo ID with the application. Emergency absentee, two kinds. (1) An employer unexpectedly requires you to be unavailable on Election Day, you are caregiver for someone who needs emergency treatment by a doctor within five days of the election, or a family member (to the second degree) dies within five days of the election: you can apply after the regular deadline, but 'no later than 5 PM on the day before the election,' Monday, November 2. (2) Your own medical emergency needing a doctor's treatment within five days of the election: the doctor certifies it on the application, you can name someone to handle the application and ballot for you, and 'the voted absentee ballot must be returned no later than noon on the day the election is held,' November 3.

return_deadline.time: Mail: received by noon on Tuesday, November 3. Hand delivery: in the Absentee Election Manager's office by close of business, and no later than 5 PM, on Monday, November 2. Postmarks do not count for regular absentee voters (only for military and overseas UOCAVA voters).

return_options: Mail it (USPS or a commercial carrier like FedEx/UPS) to the Absentee Election Manager so it arrives by noon on Tuesday, Nov 3
Hand-deliver your own ballot to the Absentee Election Manager's office by close of business (no later than 5 PM) on Monday, Nov 2
No drop boxes exist in Alabama
Nobody else may return your ballot for you; the only exception is a designee you name on a medical-emergency application
mail_ballot.postage: You pay the postage to mail your ballot back; the pre-addressed return envelope is not prepaid. The exact amount depends on the ballot's weight. Follow the instructions in your packet or ask the Absentee Election Manager. (Amount not confirmed this run; the official Voter Guide and absentee page do not state it.)
mail_ballot.signature_witness_rules: Two separate steps, and both are strict. (1) With your application: include 'a copy of valid photo identification.' Military and overseas (UOCAVA) voters are exempt. Voters 65 or older and voters with disabilities who check the 'physically incapacitated [ID Not Required]' box on the application are also exempt under the federal Voting Accessibility for the Elderly and Handicapped Act. (2) On the ballot affidavit envelope: fill it out completely, then sign it in front of either a notary public or two witnesses who are 18 or older, and have the notary or both witnesses sign. The official rule: 'An absentee ballot cannot be counted unless the affidavit is notarized or has the signatures of two witnesses who are 18 years old or older. Electronic or remote notarization of absentee ballot affidavits is not allowed.' Then: ballot in the plain secrecy envelope, secrecy envelope in the affidavit envelope, affidavit envelope in the outer pre-addressed envelope.
mail_ballot.cure_process: No general fix-it (cure) process. If the affidavit envelope is missing a signature, a notary seal, or a second witness, the ballot is not counted and you are not contacted in time to fix it. One narrow exception: if you forgot the photo ID copy with your application, you get a provisional absentee ballot, and it counts only if you get a valid photo ID to the Board of Registrars by 5 PM on Friday, November 6. Check the envelope twice before you seal it.
mail_ballot.mail_cutoff_advice: Don't trust the mail in the final week. The rule is in hand by noon on Election Day, and the Secretary of State recommends mailing 'at least two weeks before' the deadline. A ballot that arrives at 12:05 PM on November 3 is not counted. In the last few days, hand-deliver your own ballot to the Absentee Election Manager by close of business (5 PM) Monday, November 2.

early_in_person.hours_note: Alabama has no early voting. The closest thing: if you have one of the absentee excuses, go to your county's Absentee Election Manager office (usually the Circuit Clerk; in Mobile County, confirm the location through the SOS lookup), apply in person, and vote your ballot there the same day. That option ends Thursday, October 29, during regular office hours. Without an excuse, your only option is your assigned polling place on November 3.

election_day.in_line_rule: If you are in line by 7:00 PM, you get to vote. The official Voter Guide: 'Anyone who attempts to join the voting line after 7:00 P.M. shall not be permitted to vote.' Hours are local time; Mobile and nearly all of Alabama are on Central Time (a few polling places near the Georgia line run on Eastern).

accepted: Valid Alabama driver's license, including the ALEA Digital Driver's License (not expired, or expired less than 60 days)
Valid Alabama non-driver ID, including the ALEA Digital Non-Driver ID (not expired, or expired less than 60 days)
Alabama free Photo Voter ID card (from any county Board of Registrars; home visits available at 1-800-274-VOTE)

Valid state-issued ID from Alabama or any other state (the SOS lists examples: a pistol permit with photo, an AL Department of Corrections release temporary ID with photo, an AL jail movement/booking sheet with photo)
Valid employee ID with photo from the federal government, State of Alabama, a county, municipality, board, or other entity of this state
Valid student or employee ID from a public or private college or university in Alabama (including postgraduate technical or professional schools)
Valid student or employee ID issued by a state institution of higher learning in any other state
NOT accepted: utility bills, bank statements, Social Security cards, or any ID without a photo
id_rules.no_id_option: Two ways. (1) If your name is on the poll list and you are 'positively identified by at least two election officials,' you vote a regular ballot. (2) Otherwise you vote a provisional ballot, and it counts only if you bring a valid photo ID to your county Board of Registrars by 5 PM on Friday, November 6. Don't have any photo ID? A free Alabama Photo Voter ID card is available at the Board of Registrars before Election Day; call 1-800-274-VOTE (8683) for locations or a home visit.

in_the_booth.phones_detail: Yes, with limits. The official 2026 Voter Guide FAQ (p. 16): 'Can I take a cell phone into my polling place? Yes. However, use of the phone in the polling place should not disturb other voters or disrupt the polling place.' On photos: 'an individual may only take a photograph of their own ballot. Taking other photographs within the polling place may intimidate other voters and is not allowed.' Reading your notes on your phone is fine; keep it quiet and never point the camera at anyone else. Source: https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/2026-VoterGuide.pdf
in_the_booth.notes_detail: Yes, explicitly. The official 2026 Voter Guide: 'Voters may take marked sample ballots into the polling place, provided these items are for personal use only and are not disruptive to others in the polling place. The voter should not leave these items in the polling place.' Print the Mobile County sample ballot, mark it at home, and bring it. Sample ballots: https://www.sos.alabama.gov/alabama-votes/2026-general-election-sample-ballots
in_the_booth.apparel_rule: You can wear campaign gear. The official Voter Guide FAQ: 'Can I wear campaign buttons or T-shirts with political advertisements into the polling place? Yes. However, you should not loiter or leave any campaign materials in the polling place.' Active campaigning (signs, handing things out, talking people into votes) must stay 30 feet from the polling place entrance, or 30 feet from the building entrance if the polling place is inside a building. Source: https://www.sos.alabama.gov/sites/default/files/election-2026/2026-VoterGuide.pdf

gotchas.text: Registration closed Monday, October 19, and Alabama has no same-day registration. Moved within your county and didn't update in time? Go to your new polling place, update there and vote a provisional ballot.
gotchas.short: Alabama has no same-day registration, so the Oct 19 deadline is final.

gotchas.text: There is no early voting. If you can't vote on November 3, absentee voting with an excuse is your only option. Mailed applications had to arrive by Tuesday, October 27. You can still apply in person at your county's absentee office through Thursday, October 29, and vote there in the same trip. Bring a copy of your photo ID. Mobile County: Absentee Election Manager, 151 Government St, 251-574-6400. After October 29, only emergency applications are open: for most emergencies until 5 PM Monday, November 2, and for your own medical emergency, with a doctor's certification, the ballot is due by noon on November 3.
gotchas.short: No early voting; with an excuse, apply and vote absentee in person through Oct 29.

gotchas.text: An absentee ballot has two traps: a copy of your photo ID goes with the application, and the ballot envelope needs a notary or two adult witnesses (remote notarization not allowed). There is no fix-it process. Mail it so it arrives by noon on Election Day (postmarks don't count), or hand-deliver it yourself by 5 PM Monday, November 2. No drop boxes, and nobody can drop it off for you.
gotchas.short: Include a photo ID copy, and get a notary or two adult witnesses.

gotchas.text: Photo ID is required at the polls. A utility bill or bank statement does not work in Alabama. A driver's license expired less than 60 days is OK; the ALEA digital license is OK; a student ID from an Alabama college is OK. No ID means a provisional ballot that only counts if you show ID at the Board of Registrars by 5 PM Friday, November 6.
gotchas.short: Bring photo ID; a utility bill or bank statement won't work.

gotchas.text: Straight-ticket voting: filling in one party's 'straight party' oval at the top votes for that party's candidate in every partisan race on your ballot, including the judges (Alabama elects judges with party labels). You can still override any single race by marking a different candidate there; the individual mark wins. The straight-ticket oval does not vote on the four statewide amendments, Mobile County's Local Amendment 1, or the Pay-As-You-Go road question (FOR or AGAINST, titled "Special County Election," the last item on the ballot). You have to mark each one yourself or it's left blank.
gotchas.short: The straight-party oval skips the amendments and the road question, so mark those yourself.

situations.question: I moved to a new address in Alabama.
situations.short: If you moved within your county, update at your new polling place and vote a provisional ballot.
situations.answer: The deadline to update your registration was Monday, October 19, and you can't vote at your old polling place. If you moved within your county, go to your new polling place, update there and vote a provisional ballot.
steps: Moved to a different county? Registering there for this election closed October 19.
Find your new polling place at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov, or call your county Board of Registrars (Mobile County: 251-574-8586).
Bring a valid photo ID.

situations.question: I moved out of Alabama.
situations.short: Register in your new state instead; some still take registrations or offer same-day registration.
situations.answer: You vote where you live now, so register in your new state instead. Some states still take registrations or offer same-day registration, so check today.
steps: Look up your new state's rules and deadline at vote.gov.
When you register, list your old Alabama address so your old registration can be canceled.

situations.question: I'm not registered yet.
situations.short: After Oct 19, new registrations are too late for this election, so check whether you're already registered.
situations.answer: Registration for November 3 closed October 19, and Alabama has no same-day registration. Check your existing record first.
steps: Check first at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov in case you're already registered.
Not registered? Register now for future elections, online or on paper (Mobile County Board of Registrars: 151 Government St, Suite 165).

situations.question: The lookup can’t find me.
situations.short: The lookup needs your name exactly as registered: try your last name with the hyphen, a space, and joined.
situations.answer: Alabama’s lookup asks for your name and birth date. Its no-match message is “No Matching Registrants”, so try the spellings below one at a time.
steps: Try your last name with the hyphen, with a space instead, and run together, and leave out any middle name or suffix.
Still nothing? Call your county election office. A failed search doesn’t mean you’re not registered; records can lag.

situations.question: I went to the wrong polling place.
situations.short: Go to your assigned polling place; a provisional ballot cast at the wrong one won't count.
situations.answer: Go to your assigned polling place. In Alabama a provisional ballot only counts if you're a qualified voter at the polling place where you cast it, so one cast at the wrong place won't count.
steps: Look up your polling place at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov (My Voting Information).
Polls are open 7 AM to 7 PM.
Still unsure? Call the Mobile County Board of Registrars at 251-574-8586.

situations.question: My absentee ballot never came, or I lost it.
situations.short: Vote a provisional ballot at your polling place on Election Day, and bring a valid photo ID.
situations.answer: You can vote a provisional ballot at your polling place on Election Day if you never got your absentee ballot or didn't send it back. Bring a valid photo ID.
steps: Check your absentee status at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov.
Or call your county's Absentee Election Manager to ask about your options before Election Day (Mobile County: 251-574-6400).

situations.question: I made a mistake on my ballot.
situations.short: Ask a poll worker for a replacement; on an absentee ballot, call your Absentee Election Manager before sending it.
situations.answer: At the polls, take the ballot to a poll worker and ask for a replacement; they'll set the old one aside as spoiled. For an absentee ballot, call your county's Absentee Election Manager (Mobile County: 251-574-6400) before you send it.

situations.question: I applied to vote absentee, but I want to vote in person.
situations.short: If you haven't returned it, vote a provisional ballot at your polling place; if you have, you've voted.
situations.answer: If you haven't returned your absentee ballot, you can vote a provisional ballot at your polling place on Election Day. If you already returned it, you've voted.
steps: Bring a valid photo ID.
Check your absentee status at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov.

situations.question: I don't have an ID.
situations.short: If two poll workers can identify you, you vote normally; if not, vote provisionally and show ID by Nov 6.
situations.answer: Alabama requires photo ID, but you can still vote a regular ballot if two poll workers can positively identify you. Otherwise you'll vote a provisional ballot, which counts only if you bring a valid photo ID to the Board of Registrars by 5 PM on Friday, November 6.
steps: Get a free Alabama Photo Voter ID at the Board of Registrars before Election Day, or call 1-800-274-8683 for a home visit.
A license expired less than 60 days, the ALEA digital license, or an Alabama college student ID all count.
Utility bills and bank statements don't count.

situations.question: My name changed since I registered.
situations.short: Call the Board of Registrars before Election Day to ask what to bring.
situations.answer: The deadline to update your registration for this election was Monday, October 19. Call the Board of Registrars before Election Day to ask what to bring.
steps: Mobile County Board of Registrars: 251-574-8586.

situations.question: I'm a college student.
situations.short: Away at school counts as an absentee excuse; apply in person through Oct 29, since mailed applications closed.
situations.answer: Registered at home but away at school? Being a student who lives outside your county is a valid excuse to vote absentee. Mailed applications had to arrive by Tuesday, October 27. You can still apply in person at your county's absentee office through Thursday, October 29, and vote there in the same visit.
steps: Send a copy of your photo ID with the application.
The ballot envelope needs a notary or two adult witnesses.
It must arrive by noon on November 3; postmarks don't count. An Alabama college ID works as photo ID at the polls.

situations.question: I'll be away on Election Day.
situations.short: Apply and vote absentee in person at your county's absentee office through Thursday, Oct 29.
situations.answer: Alabama has no early voting, but being away from your county is a valid absentee excuse. Mailed applications had to arrive by Tuesday, October 27. You can still apply in person at your county's absentee office through Thursday, October 29, and vote there. Bring a copy of your photo ID. After that, applications are open only for certain emergencies, until 5 PM Monday, November 2 (a medical emergency with a doctor's certification has until noon on November 3).
steps: Include a copy of your photo ID with the application.
Have the ballot envelope notarized or signed by two adult witnesses.
Mailed ballots must arrive by noon on November 3; hand-deliver your own by 5 PM on Monday, November 2.

situations.question: I'm in line when the polls close.
situations.short: Stay in line: if you're in line by 7 PM, you get to vote.
situations.answer: Stay in line. If you're in line by 7 PM you get to vote, but anyone who joins the line after 7 PM can't.

situations.question: I'm worried about the signature or witnesses on my absentee ballot.
situations.short: Check it twice before sealing: you sign, plus a notary or two adult witnesses, because there's no fix-it process.
situations.answer: Check it twice before you seal it, because Alabama has no general fix-it process. The affidavit envelope must be signed by you and either notarized or signed by two witnesses who are 18 or older; remote notarization isn't allowed.
steps: Made a mistake on the envelope? Call your county's Absentee Election Manager before you send it (Mobile County: 251-574-6400).
Forgot the photo ID copy with your application? Get a valid photo ID to the Board of Registrars by 5 PM on Friday, November 6.

situations.question: They told me to vote a provisional ballot.
situations.short: It counts once the registrars confirm you're qualified there; if it was about ID, bring photo ID by Nov 6.
situations.answer: It counts once the Board of Registrars confirms you're a qualified voter at that polling place and any other requirement is met. If it was because of photo ID, bring a valid photo ID to the Board of Registrars by 5 PM on Friday, November 6.
steps: Make sure you're at your own assigned polling place first.
To check on it afterward, call the Mobile County Board of Registrars at 251-574-8586.

situations.question: How do I check that my ballot was counted?
situations.short: Check your absentee ballot at VoterView; for a provisional ballot, call your county Board of Registrars.
situations.answer: Check your absentee ballot status at myinfo.alabamavotes.gov (VoterView). For a provisional ballot, call your county Board of Registrars after the election.

judicial_review.how_judges_get_here: Alabama judges run with party labels. You choose a candidate for each seat. A straight-party vote includes judicial candidates of that party.
judicial_review.who_reviews: We found no official election job review or Alabama State Bar rating for the judges in this guide as of October 19, 2026.
judicial_review.what_the_rating_means: There is no verified current performance rating to show. Party labels identify the candidate’s party, not judicial qualifications.
judicial_review.what_it_doesnt_mean: No published rating does not mean a candidate is unqualified. A party label or endorsement is not a performance review.
judicial_review.to_keep_a_judge: Vote for the candidate you want. The candidate with the most votes wins; these are not yes-or-no retention questions.
judicial_review.history: Most judicial races on the Mobile ballot have one listed candidate. You can still read the ballot and candidate background before choosing.
